source_refs.note: Unnumbered topic Measuring performance using profiling tools as printed (PDF 70, printed 66); its own lesson since 2026-10-29 (one lesson per book heading), moved from the topic 5.3 lesson.

blocks.text: Profiling tools track the execution time and memory usage of different functions in a program. Python provides modules like cProfile and timeit for this purpose. These tools generate reports showing which parts of the code are slow or resource-intensive (as shown in Figure 5.3). Measuring performance helps prioritize areas for optimization.

blocks.alt: A profiler report table with columns Function, Call Count, Time, Cumulative Time and Description. Rows: process_data 10, 2.500, 2.500, Bottleneck; read_file 1, 2.400, 2.400, Bottleneck, highlighted in red with a warning sign; analyze_results 10, 0.100, 0.100. A dashed arrow leads to a magnifying glass over a flame.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.3: Diagram showing profiling output highlighting bottlenecks (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.3).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 5.3 shifts the column headings, with function names under 'Call Count' and call counts under 'Time'; the correct headings are Function, Call Count, Time, Cumulative Time and Description, as drawn above.
